'''Petr Čársky''' (also spelled '''Peter Čársky'''; born 29 May 1942) is a Slovak [[quantum chemistry|quantum chemist]].
 
==Life==
Čársky was born on 29 May 1942 in [[Banská Bystrica]].<ref name="iaqms">[http://www.iaqms.org/members/carsky.php IAQMS biography]</ref> He obtained in 1968 his Ph.D. at [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]], [[Prague]].
 
He worked as senior researcher at the [[Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry]], [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]], Prague (1989–1990). He became in 1990 Theoretical group leader, Jaroslav Heyrovský Institute of Physical Chemistry, [[Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic]], Prague.<ref name="iaqms"/>

== Research ==
Development of [[quantum chemistry|quantum-chemical methods]] in general. In particular:
* Multireference [[coupled cluster]] 
* Electron-molecule [[scattering theory]] and its applications to [[high resolution electron energy loss spectroscopy]] 
* Ab initio calculations on molecules with unusual bonding.<ref name="iaqms"/>

== Awards and honors ==
* Fellow of the [[Czech Learned Society]] (1994).<ref name="iaqms"/>
* [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] (1994)
